title: Campilot shell
brief: Redesign the Campilot (Rust + egui CAM app) desktop shell after the visual and structural concept extracted from the reference app Prancheta CNC: one line-weight icon language, a graphite canvas that outranks the panels, named workflow stages with gates, a collapsible inspector, and teaching strings inside the tool.

artboards.title: 2D shell — app bar, stage bar, labelled palette, collapsible inspector, status bar
artboards.tradeoff: One screen, one job: the operator always knows the next step, but the palette can only show one stage of commands at a time and experts pay a stage switch.

artboards.title: The staged workflow and its gates
artboards.tradeoff: Gates turn 'looks done' into a checkable fact and teach the app through its own help panel; the cost is a linear path that fits sign work but not exploration.

artboards.title: Icon set — 66 glyphs on one 24 × 24 grid
artboards.tradeoff: A single stroke weight reads as one hand and never shimmers when selection moves; the cost is that no icon can carry fine detail, so complex strategies rely on labels.

artboards.title: Visual tokens — dark and light, two signals, type and geometry
artboards.tradeoff: Two signal colours keep cut and selection unambiguous in monochrome and for colour-blind operators; the cost is a monochrome UI that needs icon quality to carry the personality.
